symbols.name: E
symbols.def: Each \(\mathcal E_i\subseteq\mathbb R\) is Borel and carries the relative Euclidean topology.

symbols.name: EY
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E_Y\subseteq\mathbb R\) is Borel and carries the relative Euclidean topology.

symbols.name: H
symbols.def: \(H_i\) is the union of the observational support of \(X_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)}\) and the parent-vector supports reached by recursive solutions under targets \(q=(S,s)\in Q\) for which \(i\notin S\).

symbols.name: HY
symbols.def: \(H_Y\) is the union of the observational support of \(X\) and the treatment-vector supports reached by recursive solutions under targets in \(Q\).

symbols.name: f
symbols.sig: \(f_i:\prod_{j\in\operatorname{Pa}(i)}\mathcal E_j\to\mathbb R,\ i\in I\), with each \(f_i\) Borel measurable

symbols.name: Mprime
symbols.space: the same structural space as \(\mathcal M\)

symbols.name: C
symbols.def: \(\mathsf C_0(R,Q)\) holds exactly when \(\forall i\in I\) either \(\operatorname{Pa}(i)=\varnothing\), or \(\forall p\in H_i\) there are \(r\in R\) and \(a\in\mathcal A_r\) with \(i\notin T_r\), \(\operatorname{Pa}(i)\subseteq T_r\), and \(a_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)}=p\); and, separately, \(H_Y\subseteq\mathcal A_Y^{\mathrm{src}}\).

symbols.name: mui
symbols.def: If \(\operatorname{Pa}(i)=\varnothing\), then \(\mu_i(\varnothing)=\int x_i\,dP^{\mathrm{obs}}(x,y)\); otherwise \(\mu_i(p)=\int x_i\,dP^{r,a}(x,y)\) for any covering pair \(r,a\).

symbols.name: muY
symbols.def: For \(x\in H_Y\), \(\mu_Y(x)=\int y\,dP_Y^{\mathrm{full},x}(y)\) if \(x\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{full}}\); otherwise choose any \(r\in R\) with \(T_r=I\) and \(x\in\mathcal A_r\), and set \(\mu_Y(x)=\int y\,dP^{r,x}(y)\).

symbols.name: Tq
symbols.def: For \(q=(S,s)\), visit \(i\in I\) in order \(\operatorname{ord}\), set \(Z_i=s_i\) if \(i\in S\), set \(Z_i=\mu_i(Z_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)})+e_i\) otherwise, set \(W=\mu_Y(Z)+e_Y\), and put \(T_q(e)=(Z,W)\).

symbols.name: W4
symbols.role: The pair \(\mathsf W_4(c,\delta)=(\mathcal M^0,\mathcal M^1)\) constructed from the signed four-row table in the witness-pair definition.

symbols.name: SQ
symbols.type: finite collection of intervention target sets for inference

symbols.name: Q0
symbols.type: compact intervention class used for inference
symbols.def: \(Q_0=\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal S_Q}\{S\}\times K_S\), with the disjoint-union Euclidean metric.

symbols.name: B2
symbols.space: set of real maps on \(E\times\mathcal E_Y\)
symbols.def: \(\mathcal B_2=\{\widetilde b|_{E\times\mathcal E_Y}:\widetilde b\in C_b^2(\mathbb R^{d+1}),\max_{0\leq |\alpha|\leq2}\|D^\alpha\widetilde b\|_\infty\leq1\}\)

symbols.name: InferenceHandle
symbols.role: Fit local-polynomial regime means off fold, form complete observational residual vectors off fold, resample those vectors jointly, propagate them through the target recursion, and differentiate this explicit composition to obtain the one-step correction and a common exchangeable bootstrap.

standard.name: Compact covariate domains for uniform nonparametric regression
Compact covariate domain for counterfactual regression

assumptions.condition: \(\bigwedge_{i\in I:\operatorname{Pa}(i)\ne\varnothing}\bigl[\exists O_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{|\operatorname{Pa}(i)|}\text{ open},\ H_i\subseteq O_i,\ \exists g_i\in\mathcal H^{s_i}(O_i,L_{\mathrm{reg}}):h_i=g_i|_{H_i}\bigr]\bigr)\).
\(\exists O_Y\subseteq\mathbb R^d\text{ open},\ H_Y\subseteq O_Y,\ \exists g_Y\in\mathcal H^{s_Y}(O_Y,L_{\mathrm{reg}}):h_Y=g_Y|_{H_Y}\).

standard.name: Compact support for a counterfactual input process

definitions.name: Borel confounded additive-noise class
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak M(G,H,H_Y)=\{\mathcal M=(G,f,f_Y,P_U):\operatorname{ord}\in\operatorname{TopSort}(G),\ f_i\text{ is Borel measurable for every }i\in I,\ f_Y\text{ is Borel measurable},\ X_i=f_i(X_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)})+U_i,\ Y=f_Y(X)+U_Y,\ E_{P_U}\|U\|_2^2<\infty,\text{ and }\mathscr D\text{ has surgical intervention semantics}\}\).

definitions.name: Exact recursive support cover
definitions.construction: \(\mathsf C_0(R,Q)=\bigl[\forall i\in I:\operatorname{Pa}(i)=\varnothing\ \lor\ \forall p\in H_i\ \exists r\in R\ \exists a\in\mathcal A_r:\ i\notin T_r,\operatorname{Pa}(i)\subseteq T_r,a_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)}=p\bigr]\land[H_Y\subseteq\mathcal A_Y^{\mathrm{src}}]\).

definitions.name: Regime-source mean map
definitions.construction: \(\mu_i(\varnothing)=\int x_i\,dP^{\mathrm{obs}}(x,y)\) when \(\operatorname{Pa}(i)=\varnothing\); \(\mu_i(p)=\int x_i\,dP^{r,a}(x,y)\) for a covering pair when \(\operatorname{Pa}(i)\ne\varnothing\); and, for \(x\in H_Y\), \(\mu_Y(x)=\int y\,dP_Y^{\mathrm{full},x}(y)\) when \(x\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{full}}\), or \(\mu_Y(x)=\int y\,dP^{r,x}(y)\) for any \(r\in R\) with \(T_r=I\) and \(x\in\mathcal A_r\).

definitions.name: Topological residual pushforward
definitions.construction: For \(q=(S,s)\), draw \(e\sim\nu_{\mathscr D}\), recurse in \(\operatorname{ord}\) using \(Z_i=s_i\) on \(S\) and \(Z_i=\mu_i(Z_{\operatorname{Pa}(i)})+e_i\) off \(S\), set \(W=\mu_Y(Z)+e_Y\), and return \(\Lambda_q=\mathcal L(Z,W)=(T_q)_{\#}\nu_{\mathscr D}\).

definitions.name: Four-point Rademacher necessity pair
definitions.construction: Let \(A\) and \(B\) be independent Rademacher signs, let \(e_1,e_{d+1}\) be the first and last coordinate vectors of \(\mathbb R^{d+1}\), and set \(\varepsilon_{ab}=\eta(ae_1+be_{d+1})\) for \((a,b)\in\{-1,1\}^2\), where \(\eta>0\). Both models use \(P_U=4^{-1}\sum_{a,b}\delta_{\varepsilon_{ab}}\), which is centered, bounded, non-Gaussian, and has exactly four atoms. For a failed nonroot certificate \(c=(i,p_\star,q_\star)\), where \(q_\star\) leaves \(i\) free and reaches \(p_\star\), assign the baseline structural tables in topological order so that every observational row and every supplied-regime row in which \(i\) is free avoids \(p_\star\); supplied regimes with \(i\in T_r\), including every \(T_r=I\) regime, do not evaluate \(h_i\). Take \(h^1_j=h^0_j\) for \(j\ne i\), \(h_i^1(p)=h_i^0(p)+\delta\mathbf 1\{p=p_\star\}\), and \(h_Y^1=h_Y^0\). For a failed outcome certificate \(c=(Y,x_\star,q_\star)\), one has \(x_\star\in H_Y\setminus\mathcal A_Y^{\mathrm{src}}\). Assign the same four baseline rows so that the observational and every nonfull supplied regime avoid \(x_\star\); every supplied regime with \(T_r=I\) and the distinguished full-intervention family exclude \(x_\star\) from their assignment domains. Take \(h^1=h^0\) and \(h_Y^1(x)=h_Y^0(x)+\delta\mathbf 1\{x=x_\star\}\). Finally put \(f^k=h^k\), \(f_Y^k=h_Y^k\), and \(P_U^k=P_U\) for \(k\in\{0,1\}\).

definitions.name: Compact intervention and smooth-AOI classes
definitions.construction: \(Q_0=\bigcup_{S\in\mathcal S_Q}\{S\}\times K_S\), \(\mathcal T_0=[t_-,t_+]\), and \(\mathcal B_2=\{\widetilde b|_{E\times\mathcal E_Y}:\widetilde b\in C_b^2(\mathbb R^{d+1}),\max_{0\leq|\alpha|\leq2}\|D^\alpha\widetilde b\|_\infty\leq1\}\).

definitions.name: Cross-fitted joint-residual-resampling construction
definitions.construction: Partition each regime sample into common folds; on complementary folds fit local-polynomial \(\widehat\mu_i\) on the Euclidean parent coordinates and fit \(\widehat\mu_Y\) by pooling the distinguished full-intervention sample with every supplied regime satisfying \(T_r=I\), using the declared ambient Hölder extensions. For each held-out observational unit form \(\widehat e_k=((X_{ik}^0-\widehat\mu_i(X_{\operatorname{Pa}(i),k}^0))_{i\in I},Y_k^0-\widehat\mu_Y(X_k^0))\); push the empirical law of the complete vectors \(\widehat e_k\) through the fitted \(T_q\); for \(b\in\mathcal B_2\) differentiate this explicit regression--empirical-law--recursion composition and add its foldwise one-step correction; for CDFs use \(\mathbf 1\{W\leq t\}\), \((q,t)\in Q_0\times\mathcal T_0\), and denote the resulting empirical CDF by \(\widehat F_q(t)\); and repeat all fits, residuals, and pushforwards under one set of exchangeable bootstrap weights.

statements.statement: If \(\mathsf C_0(R,Q)\) holds, then for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(G,H,H_Y)\), \(\mu_i(\varnothing)=E[X_i]=h_i(\varnothing)\) for each root \(i\), \(\mu_i(p)=h_i(p)\) for each nonroot \(i\) and \(p\in H_i\), and \(\mu_Y(x)=h_Y(x)\) for \(x\in H_Y\). The treatment value is invariant to the covering pair \(r,a\), and the outcome value is invariant across the distinguished full-intervention family and every supplied regime with \(T_r=I\) and \(x\in\mathcal A_r\).
statements.justification: Roots are recovered observationally; nonroots use parent-fixing means; and outcome means may come from any supplied full-treatment source.
statements.gap: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (2025), equation (17), supplies the Gaussian shifted-mechanism calculation; this lemma is the mechanism-recovery component of the full-law theorem.
statements.consumer: The recovered centered maps are the deterministic inputs to residual extraction and every covered target recursion.

statements.statement: If \(\mathsf C_0(R,Q)\) holds, then \(r_{\mathscr D}(X,Y)=\varepsilon\) almost surely under \(P^{\mathrm{obs}}\), and therefore \(\nu_{\mathscr D}=\mathcal L_{P_U}(U-E_{P_U}U)\). Thus \(\mathscr D\) identifies the complete centered joint disturbance law, including cross-node dependence and non-Gaussian features.
statements.justification: The vector residual law, rather than a covariance matrix, is the object that removes Gaussianity.
statements.gap: Jeunen et al. (2022), Section 4, estimates Gaussian noise parameters; this lemma isolates the residual-law component required by the full-law theorem.
statements.consumer: Joint residual resampling preserves latent confounding when unseen intervention combinations are propagated.

statements.statement: If \(\mathsf C_0(R,Q)\) holds, then for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M(G,H,H_Y)\), every \(q\in Q\), and every bounded Borel \(b\), \(\mathcal L_{\mathcal M}((X,Y)^q)=\Lambda_q=(T_q)_{\#}\nu_{\mathscr D}\) and \(E_{\mathcal M}[b((X,Y)^q)]=\theta_{q,b}\). This is a strict full-law strengthening of Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (2025), Theorem 2: on its Gaussian mean-functional specialization the pushforward yields its identified average outcome, while for arbitrary dependent Borel \(P_U\) it additionally identifies every bounded distributional functional.
statements.justification: A finite experimental cover identifies every covered intervention law rather than only a collection of means.
statements.gap: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (2025), Theorem 2, identifies an average outcome under Gaussian confounded additive noise; it does not identify the complete postintervention law under arbitrary dependent Borel disturbances.
statements.consumer: Policy analysts can evaluate tail risk, quantiles, stochastic dominance, and bounded welfare criteria for unseen covered intervention combinations.

statements.statement: For each failed nonroot parent-cell certificate or failed outcome-source-cell certificate and sufficiently small \(\delta>0\), the explicit construction \(\mathsf W_4(c,\delta)\) produces two members \(\mathcal M^0,\mathcal M^1\in\mathfrak M(G,H,H_Y)\). Each centered disturbance law is uniform on exactly four distinct bounded atoms; the models agree on \(P^{\mathrm{obs}}\), on every \(P^{r,a}\) including every supplied regime with \(T_r=I\), and on every distinguished \(P_Y^{\mathrm{full},x}\), yet their designated target laws differ.
statements.justification: This membership-and-matching lemma makes the four-point witness an exhibited construction rather than a promised proof device.
statements.gap: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (2025), Appendix A.3, uses a Gaussian null-set modification rather than a bounded non-Gaussian pair matching the entire regime tuple.
statements.consumer: The lemma supplies auditable counterexamples for experimental designs that miss either structural component of the cover.

statements.statement: The exact condition \(\mathsf C_0(R,Q)\) is equivalent to a uniform identification guarantee for \(\{\Lambda_q:q\in Q\}\) from \(\mathscr D\) over \(\mathfrak M(G,H,H_Y)\). Sufficiency is Theorem 1. For necessity, failure of the nonroot parent-cell clause invokes the treatment version of \(\mathsf W_4\), whereas failure of \(H_Y\subseteq\mathcal A_Y^{\mathrm{src}}\) invokes its outcome version. In either case two bounded four-atom non-Gaussian SCMs agree simultaneously on the observational law, every supplied-regime law including all regimes with \(T_r=I\), and the distinguished full-intervention family, but differ under a target \(q\), so a bounded Borel \(b\) separates their values of \(\theta_{q,b}\). This exact value-specific frontier is not supplied by the sufficient graph-level intervention covers of Kandasamy, Bhattacharyya, and Honavar (2019) or the unrestricted graphical data-fusion criterion of Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (2020).
statements.justification: Separate witnesses for the treatment and outcome clauses make the cover an exact uniform design frontier.
statements.gap: Published Gaussian mean results and graph-level cover results do not provide a necessary-and-sufficient value-specific frontier certified by a bounded non-Gaussian pair matching the enlarged complete regime tuple.
statements.consumer: Experimental planners obtain a certificate that each omitted nonroot parent cell or outcome cell requires additional information for a uniform guarantee.

statements.statement: If \(\nu_{\mathscr D}\) has Lebesgue density \(p_\varepsilon\), then every pushed-forward outcome law is atomless: \(\sup_{q\in Q_0}\sup_{t\in\mathcal T_0}\Lambda_q(E\times\{t\})=0\).
statements.justification: The triangular additive recursion has unit slope in the outcome residual, so absolute continuity yields the explicit no-atom property needed for CDF linearization.
statements.gap: Counterfactual-distribution inference commonly assumes atomlessness; here it is derived from the identified residual density and the additive pushforward.
statements.consumer: The derived continuity condition supports uniform distributional bands without adding a redundant model assumption.

statements.statement: Using the construction \(\mathrm{InferenceHandle}\), determine the sharp inequalities relating \(s_i\), \(s_Y\), the parent dimensions \(|\operatorname{Pa}(i)|\), and \(d\) that suffice for both of the following conclusions on the declared classes. First, for every fixed \(q\in Q_0\) and \(b\in\mathcal B_2\), derive the canonical gradient of \(\theta_{q,b}\) in the multi-regime model and prove that the cross-fitted one-step estimator is asymptotically linear and attains its semiparametric variance bound. Second, prove conditional weak convergence of the common exchangeable bootstrap for \(\sqrt n(\widehat F_q(t)-F_q(t))\) in \(\ell^\infty(Q_0\times\mathcal T_0)\), and hence simultaneous distributional-band coverage.
statements.justification: The compact metric index set, smooth AOI ball, density conditions, and explicit estimator now make efficiency and uniform bootstrap claims mathematically determinate.
statements.gap: Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, and Melly (2013), Theorems 4.1--5.2, treat regression counterfactual operators, not a recursive multi-regime pushforward driven by shared generated residual vectors.
statements.consumer: The International Stroke Trial semi-synthetic benchmark of Jeunen et al. can report calibrated methodological uncertainty without asserting a new clinical aspirin effect.

sampling_model.design: A fixed finite collection of hard-intervention families, including any supplied regimes with \(T_r=I\), together with the observational regime and a distinguished full-treatment intervention family.
sampling_model.units: Independent units within and across regimes, with regime sample proportions converging to positive constants.
sampling_model.treatment: For regime \(r\), \(T_r\) is fixed to \(a\in\mathcal A_r\); target interventions are \(q=(S,s)\in Q\), and inference is indexed by the compact subclass \(Q_0\).
sampling_model.overlap: The exact deterministic cover \(\mathsf C_0(R,Q)\) uses every full-treatment source for population identification; assignment-density overlap on compact Euclidean envelopes governs nonparametric inference.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Cross-fitted local-polynomial estimation of nonroot regime means and pooled outcome-source means under ambient Euclidean extensions, observational averaging for roots, and out-of-fold joint-residual resampling.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 2 identifies the average outcome under interventions in its Gaussian confounded additive-noise model.
Theorem 2 identifies conditional single-treatment effects in the symmetric additive multivariate-Gaussian model.
Theorem 1 identifies joint nonlinear mean effects from observational and singleton-intervention distributions under additive Gaussian noise.
The g-identification procedure is sound and complete for causal effects from arbitrary surrogate experiments in unrestricted graphical models.
The paper formulates a graph-level minimum intervention cover sufficient for graph-identifiable effects and relates it to do-calculus completeness.
Theorems 4.1--5.2 give functional limit and exchangeable-bootstrap results for regression-based counterfactual distribution operators.

tldr: For a known-DAG confounded additive-noise SCM with Borel structural maps and an arbitrary dependent Borel disturbance law, roots are recovered from observational means, nonroot mechanisms from parent-fixing regime means, and the outcome mechanism from the union of the distinguished full-intervention family and every supplied regime with \(T_r=I\). Observational vector residuals identify the complete centered disturbance law, and a topological pushforward identifies every covered intervention distribution and bounded AOI. The exact-cover theorem uses a simultaneous four-atom Rademacher pair for necessity. The statistical question is posed on relative Euclidean state spaces with explicit ambient smooth extensions, density conditions, and a derived no-atom property.

project_justification.gap: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu identify a Gaussian average outcome; Jeunen et al. identify Gaussian intervention-disentangled means. Neither result identifies a complete postintervention law under arbitrary dependent Borel noise or gives an exact value-specific necessity pair matching every supplied regime, including full-treatment regimes.
project_justification.niche: Additivity makes centered mechanisms and the entire confounding vector observable through root means, parent-fixing regime means, all available full-treatment outcome-source means, and observational residuals on an exact recursive support cover.
project_justification.fill: The two novelty claims are the arbitrary-Borel full-law pushforward theorem and the exact-cover necessity frontier with a simultaneous bounded four-atom witness; the Euclidean inference layer is retained as an open-ended question.

related_work: Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (2025), Theorem 2, equation (17), and Appendix A.3 of Identification of Average Outcome under Interventions in Confounded Additive Noise Models give the closest Gaussian average-outcome and shifted-mechanism results; Theorem 1 strictly strengthens that target to arbitrary dependent Borel postintervention laws. Jeunen et al. (2022), Theorems 1 and 2, Section 4, and the conclusion inform the Gaussian and parentless regression check but are not theorem-level targets. Saengkyongam and Silva (2020), Theorem 1, likewise informs only that regression check. Lee, Correa, and Bareinboim (2020) give sound and complete graphical identification from arbitrary surrogate experiments without additive residual-law recovery. Kandasamy, Bhattacharyya, and Honavar (2019) optimize a graph-level intervention cover, distinct from the exact value-specific recursive support frontier in Theorem 2. Chernozhukov, Fernández-Val, and Melly (2013) provide the functional-limit and exchangeable-bootstrap template for counterfactual distributions, but not for a recursive map driven by generated joint residuals. The International Stroke Trial analysis in Jeunen et al. is used solely as a published semi-synthetic methodological benchmark, not as evidence for a new clinical aspirin conclusion.
technical_internal_limitation: The necessity theorem is a uniform design guarantee over the declared support envelope, not a claim that every particular law failing a direct cell has multiple representations; special discrete laws may reveal an uncovered value through additional distributional restrictions. Exact cover remains value-specific, inference fixes \(d\) and finitely many regimes, and growing graphs or approximate coverage are outside the core. Unnumbered regression corollary: when \(d=1\), \(\operatorname{Pa}(1)=\varnothing\), \(R=\varnothing\), and \(H_Y\subseteq\mathcal A_{\mathrm{full}}\), the root disjunct gives \(\mu_1(\varnothing)=E[X_1]\), the residual pushforward reproduces the observational law for the empty intervention and the supplied full-intervention outcome law for \(\operatorname{do}(X_1=x)\); its Gaussian mean restriction agrees with Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (2025), Theorem 2, and the parentless multivariate mean restriction agrees with Jeunen et al. (2022), Theorem 2. This corollary is a regression check, not a novelty claim.
honest_scope: The only theorem-level novelty claims are population full-law identification and the exact-cover necessity frontier. Mechanism recovery, residual recovery, witness validity, and atomlessness are supporting results. The Gaussian and parentless reductions appear only as an unnumbered regression corollary. The canonical gradient, sharp dimension--smoothness frontier, efficiency result, and uniform bootstrap theorem remain open. All structural maps are Borel measurable; every supplied full-treatment regime enters the outcome-source cover; smooth AOIs are restrictions of \(C_b^2(\mathbb R^{d+1})\) maps; and mechanism smoothness is defined through open-neighborhood Euclidean extensions.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorem 2 and Appendix A.3 give a Gaussian mean-level intervention-target result; equation (17) recovers shifted mechanisms from parent-fixing interventions.
seed_details.kernel: Prove that a root-corrected exact recursive support cover identifies the complete centered disturbance law and every postintervention law, with uniform necessity certified by an explicit four-point non-Gaussian pair.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Recover each root centered mechanism from its observational mean, then replace Gaussian covariance reconstruction by the observational vector-residual pushforward.
seed_details.target_method_search: The carried literature map contains no theorem identifying arbitrary Borel postintervention laws from the complete dependent residual distribution under this cover.
seed_details.red_team: The residual pushforward might appear to be a direct rewrite of the Gaussian proof.
seed_details.rebuttal: The comparator identifies Gaussian mean functionals, whereas the proposed object is the complete dependent Borel residual law and its full distributional pushforward, with a bounded non-Gaussian uniform-design converse.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Roots are observational by construction, every full-treatment source enters the outcome clause, the necessity modes are separated, and the witness is exhibited before its membership claim.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Theorems 4.1--5.2 cover regression counterfactual processes but not recursively reused generated joint residuals.
seed_details.kernel: Derive the canonical gradient and common-bootstrap limit for the cross-fitted residual pushforward on compact intervention, threshold, and smooth-AOI classes.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Linearize the joint empirical residual law and each fitted mechanism through all recursive appearances in \(T_q\).
seed_details.target_method_search: The carried literature map contains no generated joint-residual recursion spanning observational, partial-intervention, and full-intervention samples.
seed_details.red_team: The question could collapse to an ordinary counterfactual-distribution delta method.
seed_details.rebuttal: The complete residual vector is generated by multiple fitted mechanisms and then reused at every recursive node; its shared influence and bootstrap coupling are not present in the comparator operator.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The question fixes Euclidean metric index sets, ambient smooth extensions, an estimator construction, and density regularity while leaving the sharp rate frontier to the solver.

seed_details.opened_evidence: The carried evidence concerns graph-based nested identification, while the selected kernel concerns ordinary interventions.
seed_details.kernel: Characterize factual-conditioned residual-fiber identification after the ordinary intervention theorem.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Disintegrate the residual law on factual fibers before applying a covered action.
seed_details.target_method_search: No carried source combines residual-law recovery with nested counterfactual fibers.
seed_details.red_team: SCM recovery could make the target tautological.
seed_details.rebuttal: Null factual fibers and regular conditional residual laws create an additional identification problem.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The reserve seed does not alter the selected ordinary-intervention kernel.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Single-function extrapolation bounds do not impose recursive compatibility with one common residual law.
seed_details.kernel: Give sharp compatible AOI bounds under incomplete exact cover.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Propagate coupled extrapolation envelopes through the residual recursion.
seed_details.target_method_search: No carried source gives coupled sharp bounds for this SCM.
seed_details.red_team: Nodewise interval propagation may appear sufficient.
seed_details.rebuttal: Nodewise extrema need not correspond to one compatible disturbance coupling.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The reserve object is a coupled bound, not an informal robustness discussion.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Hard parent fixing reveals means directly; soft regimes require operator inversion.
seed_details.kernel: Find an operator-rank frontier for soft-regime recovery.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace evaluation by inversion of regime-contrast operators.
seed_details.target_method_search: No carried comparator supplies this rank frontier.
seed_details.red_team: Known soft regimes may be mixtures of hard regimes.
seed_details.rebuttal: The mixture operator can be noninjective and must also preserve residual dependence.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The selected proposal remains on hard interventions.

seed_details.opened_evidence: Graph-level intervention design does not recover nonlinear mechanisms with arbitrary dependent errors.
seed_details.kernel: Jointly recover the graph, mechanisms, and residual law.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Use cross-regime invariance to orient candidate parents.
seed_details.target_method_search: No carried source establishes this arbitrary-noise joint recovery.
seed_details.red_team: The known-graph theorem does not itself solve discovery.
seed_details.rebuttal: This distinct seed would require a new invariance argument and is not smuggled into the selected kernel.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Known \(G\) remains explicit in the selected core.

seed_details.opened_evidence: The comparator optimizes graph-level targets rather than recursively reached assignment values.
seed_details.kernel: Choose a minimum-cost value-specific exact cover.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Couple target reachability with the cover decision.
seed_details.target_method_search: No carried source optimizes this value-specific cover.
seed_details.red_team: After enumeration the problem resembles set cover.
seed_details.rebuttal: The universe itself changes with recursively induced target supports.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The design seed is not asserted as a result in this core.

seed_details.opened_evidence: The carried evidence gives no graph-dependent uncovered-mass sensitivity scalar.
seed_details.kernel: Derive a sign-reversal frontier under approximate cover.
seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Track contamination mass through descendants under a common residual law.
seed_details.target_method_search: No carried comparator supplies this frontier.

novelty_justification: The novelty claims are exactly Theorem 1 and Theorem 2. Theorem 1 strictly strengthens Elahi, Ghasemi, and Kocaoglu (2025), Theorem 2 of Identification of Average Outcome under Interventions in Confounded Additive Noise Models: equation (17) recovers shifted mechanisms in the Gaussian mean setting, whereas observational vector residualization identifies the complete centered Borel disturbance law and an explicit topological pushforward identifies every covered target law. Theorem 2 gives the reverse direction as an exact uniform design frontier. Its outcome clause pools the distinguished full-intervention family with every supplied regime satisfying \(T_r=I\), and both failure modes use a signed four-row Rademacher construction whose class membership and simultaneous agreement on the enlarged complete regime tuple are theorem obligations. Jeunen et al. (2022), Theorem 2, identifies conditional single-treatment effects in a symmetric Gaussian ANM and is used only to check the Gaussian parentless reduction. Mechanism recovery, residual recovery, witness validity, atomlessness, and the unnumbered Gaussian and parentless regression corollary are supporting results rather than novelty claims.
